units.literal: Again he was Secretariat Chief Clerk.

units.zh: 丁母憂。
units.en: He entered mourning for his mother.
units.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 起為武康令，固辭不免，到縣百許日，稱疾去官。
units.en: He was recalled as magistrate of Wukang, declined firmly but could not refuse, and after barely a hundred days in the county claimed illness and resigned.
units.literal: Recalled as magistrate of Wukang, he firmly declined but could not avoid it; after reaching the county about a hundred days, he claimed illness and left office.

units.zh: 服闋，除司徒左西掾，州治中從事史。
units.en: When his mourning was over he was made left western clerk to the Minister of Education (Situ) and attendant administrative officer of the province.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Left Western Clerk of the Secretariat and Attendant Administrative Officer of the province.

units.zh: 元嘉十二年，東諸郡大水，民人饑饉，吳義興及吳郡之錢唐，升米三百。
units.en: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies were flooded and the people starved. In Wu, Yixing, and Qiantang of Wu commandery, rice reached three hundred cash per sheng.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia the eastern commanderies suffered great flood; the people were in famine—in Wu, Yixing and Qiantang in Wu commandery, rice was three hundred cash per sheng.

units.zh: 以演之及尚書祠部郎江邃並兼散騎常侍，巡行拯恤，許以便宜從事。
units.en: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui of the ministry of rites were both given the additional post of routinely attached gentleman to tour the region and bring relief, with authority to act as circumstances required.
units.literal: Yanzhi and Jiang Sui, Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, were both additionally made Routinely Attached Gentlemen to tour and relieve, permitted to act as circumstances required.

units.zh: 演之乃開倉廩以賑饑民，民有生子者，口賜米一斗，刑獄有疑枉，悉制遣之，百姓蒙賴。
units.en: Yanzhi opened the granaries to feed the hungry. Families with new births received a dou of rice for each mouth, and doubtful or wrongful prisoners were all released. The people owed him their survival.
units.literal: Yanzhi then opened granaries to relieve the starving; for those who bore sons, each person was given one dou of rice; doubtful and wrongful cases in punishment and prison were all released—the people relied on him.

units.zh: 轉別駕從事史，領本郡中正，深為義康所待，故在府州前後十餘年。
units.en: He became attendant administrative officer and head of the provincial impartial judge. Deeply favored by Yikang, he remained at headquarters and in the province for more than ten years in all.
units.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Administrative Officer, heading the provincial impartial judge; deeply treated by Yikang, so at headquarters and province for more than ten years before and after.

units.zh: 後劉湛、劉斌等結黨，欲排廢尚書僕射殷景仁，演之雅仗正義，與湛等不同，湛因此讒之於義康。
units.en: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin, and others formed a faction to drive out Vice Director Yin Jingren. Yanzhi stood on principle and broke with them, and Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.
units.literal: Later Liu Zhan, Liu Bin and others formed a faction wishing to expel and ruin Vice Director Yin Jingren; Yanzhi by nature relied on righteousness and differed from Zhan and others—Zhan therefore slandered him to Yikang.

units.zh: 嘗因論事不合旨，義康變色曰：「自今而後，我不復相信！」
units.en: Once, when their discussion of policy failed to please him, Yikang turned dark and said, "From now on I will no longer trust you!"
units.literal: Once in discussion of affairs they did not accord with the intent; Yikang changed color and said, "From now on I no longer trust you!"

units.zh: 演之與景仁素善，盡心於朝庭，太祖甚嘉之，以為尚書吏部郎。
units.en: Yanzhi had long been close to Jingren and gave his full loyalty to the court. The emperor praised him highly and made him gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
units.literal: Yanzhi and Jingren had long been on good terms and devoted their hearts to the court; the Taizu greatly praised this and made him Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 十七年，義康出籓，誅湛等，以演之為右衛將軍。
units.en: In the seventeenth year Yikang left for his fief, Zhan and his faction were executed, and Yanzhi was made general of the right guards.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year Yikang went out to his fief, Zhan and others were executed, and Yanzhi was made General of the Right Guards.

units.zh: 景仁尋卒，乃以後軍長史范曄為左衛將軍，與演之對掌禁旅，同參機密。
units.en: Jingren soon died, and Fan Ye, chief clerk of the rear army, was made general of the left guards to share command of the palace guard with Yanzhi and to join him in confidential counsel.
units.literal: Jingren soon died; then Rear Army Chief Clerk Fan Ye was made General of the Left Guards to pair with Yanzhi in commanding the forbidden guard and share in secrets.

units.zh: 二十年，遷侍中，右衛將軍如故。
units.en: In the twentieth year he was made palace attendant while retaining his post as general of the right guards.
units.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant, General of the Right Guards as before.

units.zh: 太祖謂之曰：「侍中領衛，望實優顯，此蓋宰相便坐，卿其勉之。」
units.en: The emperor told him, "As palace attendant commanding the guard, your standing is eminent and bright. This is virtually the chief minister's seat. Do your utmost in it."
units.literal: The Taizu said to him, "Palace Attendant commanding the guard—reputation and substance are superior and prominent; this is virtually the chief minister's seat of honor. Strive in it."

units.zh: 上欲伐林邑，朝臣不同，唯廣州刺史陸徽與演之贊成上意。
units.en: The emperor wished to attack Linyi. Most court ministers disagreed, but Governor Lu Hui of Guangzhou and Yanzhi alone supported the plan.
units.literal: The Emperor wished to attack Linyi; court ministers differed—only Governor of Guangzhou Lu Hui and Yanzhi supported the imperial intent.

units.zh: 及平，賜群臣黃金、生口、銅器等物，演之所得偏多。
units.en: After the campaign succeeded, the emperor gave gold, captives, bronze vessels, and the like to his ministers, and Yanzhi received a larger share than most.
units.literal: When it was pacified, gold, captives, bronze vessels and such were given to the ministers—Yanzhi's share was comparatively more.

units.zh: 上謂之曰：「廟堂之謀，卿參其力，平此遠夷，未足多建茅土。
units.en: The emperor told him, "You shared in the court's planning, but pacifying these distant peoples is not enough to merit many new fiefs.
units.literal: The Emperor said to him, "In court planning you shared in the effort; pacifying these distant barbarians is not enough to build many fiefs of earth.

units.zh: 廓清京都，鳴鸞東岱，不憂河山不開也。」
units.en: When the capital is cleared and the imperial procession sounds at Mount Tai, you need not fear that the realm will not open before us."
units.literal: Clearing the capital region and sounding the imperial bells at Mount Tai—you need not worry that rivers and mountains will not open."

units.zh: 二十一年，詔曰：「總司戎政，翼贊東朝，惟允之舉，匪賢莫授。
units.en: In the twenty-first year an edict declared, "To command military affairs and aid the eastern palace is a trust given only to the worthy.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict said, "Overall command of military affairs, aiding and assisting the eastern palace—such trusted appointment is given to none but the worthy.

units.zh: 侍中領右衛將軍演之，清業貞審，器思沈濟。
units.en: Palace Attendant and general of the right guards Yanzhi is pure in conduct, firm in judgment, and deep and steady in mind.
units.literal: Palace Attendant commanding the Right Guards Yanzhi—pure conduct and faithful scrutiny, capacity and thought deep and steady.

units.zh: 右衛將軍曄，才應通敏，理懷清要。
units.en: General of the right guards Ye is quick and penetrating in talent and clear and exact in judgment.
units.literal: General of the Right Guards Ye—talent responding with penetrating keenness, reason embracing clarity and essentials.

units.zh: 並美彰出內，誠亮在公，能克懋厥猷，樹績所蒞。
units.en: Both show excellence within and integrity in public service, and are able to fulfill their duties and build achievement in every post they hold.
units.literal: Both beauty manifests within and sincerity shines in public service—able to exert their merit and establish achievement where they preside.

units.zh: 演之可中領軍，曄可太子詹事。」
units.en: Yanzhi is fit to be central commander of the army; Ye is fit to be steward of the heir apparent."
units.literal: Yanzhi may be Central Commander of the Army; Ye may be Steward of the Heir Apparent."

units.zh: 曄懷逆謀，演之覺其有異，言之太祖，曄尋事發伏誅。
units.en: Ye harbored treasonous designs. Yanzhi sensed something amiss and reported it to the emperor. Ye's plot was soon exposed and he was executed.
units.literal: Ye harbored a treacherous plot; Yanzhi sensed his strangeness and spoke to the Taizu; Ye's affair soon broke out and he was executed.

units.zh: 遷領國子祭酒，本州大中正，轉吏部尚書，領太子右衛率。
units.en: He became libationer of the national university and great impartial judge of his province, then minister of personnel and commander of the heir apparent's right guard.
units.literal: He was transferred to Libationer of the National University, Great Impartial Judge of the province, then Minister of Personnel, additionally commanding Right Guard of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 雖未為宰相，任寄不異也。
units.en: Though he was not formally chief minister, the trust placed in him was no less.
units.literal: Though not chief minister, his trust and commission were no different.

units.zh: 素有心氣，疾病歷年，上使臥疾治事。
units.en: He had long suffered from heart trouble and was ill for years, yet the emperor had him conduct affairs from his sickbed.
units.literal: He had long had heart qi ailment; illness lasted years—the Emperor had him conduct affairs while ill in bed.

units.zh: 性好舉才，申濟屈滯，而謙約自持，上賜女伎，不受。
units.en: He loved to advance talent and help those who had been passed over, yet he remained modest and restrained. When the emperor gave him female performers, he refused them.
units.literal: By nature he loved raising talent and extending help to the blocked and stalled, yet maintained modest restraint; the Emperor gifted female performers and he would not accept.

units.zh: 二十六年，車駕拜京陵，演之以疾不從。
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor went to worship at the capital tombs, but Yanzhi did not accompany him because of illness.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the imperial carriage worshipped at the capital tombs; Yanzhi from illness did not follow.

units.zh: 上還宮，召見，自勉到坐，出至尚書下省，暴卒，時年五十三。
units.en: When the emperor returned to the palace he summoned Yanzhi, who forced himself to attend. After leaving the audience he reached the lower offices of the secretariat and died suddenly, at the age of fifty-three.
units.literal: The Emperor returned to the palace and summoned him to audience; exerting himself he reached his seat; going out to the lower offices of the Secretariat he suddenly died, aged fifty-three.

units.zh: 太祖痛惜之，追贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰貞侯。
units.en: The emperor grieved deeply for him and posthumously made him routinely attached gentleman and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal, with the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.
units.literal: The Taizu grieved and prized him; posthumously he was given Routinely Attached Gentleman and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

units.zh: 演之昔與同使江邃字玄遠，濟陽考城人。
units.en: Yanzhi had once served as envoy together with Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
units.literal: Yanzhi once with fellow envoy Jiang Sui, courtesy name Xuanyuan, a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 頗有文義。
units.en: He had considerable literary learning.
units.literal: He had considerable literary understanding.

units.zh: 官至司徒記室參軍，撰《文釋》，傳於世。
units.en: He rose to recording colonel of the secretariat and wrote Literary Explication, which circulated in his day.
units.literal: He reached office as Recording Colonel of the Secretariat and composed Literary Explication, transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 演之子睦，至黃門郎，通直散騎常侍。
units.en: Yanzhi's son Mu rose to gentleman at the Yellow Gate and direct, routinely attached gentleman.
units.literal: Yanzhi's son Mu reached Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Direct and Routinely Attached Gentleman.

units.zh: 世祖大明初，坐要引上左右俞欣之訪評殿省內事，又與弟西陽王文學勃忿鬩不睦，坐徙始興郡，勃免官禁錮。
units.en: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Daming era, Mu was exiled to Shixing for drawing the emperor's attendant Yu Xin into discussions of inner-palace affairs and for feuding with his younger brother Bo, literary attendant to the prince of Xiyang. Bo was dismissed and barred from office.
units.literal: Early in Daming of Shizu, for summoning and drawing in the Emperor's attendant Yu Xin to inquire and comment on inner-palace affairs, and for quarreling with his younger brother Prince Xiyang's literary attendant Bo, he was exiled to Shixing commandery; Bo was dismissed from office and forbidden.

units.zh: 勃好為文章，善彈琴，能圍棊，而輕薄逐利。
units.en: Bo loved literary composition, played the zither well, and was adept at weiqi, yet he was frivolous and greedy for gain.
units.literal: Bo was fond of literary composition, skilled at the zither, and able at weiqi, yet frivolous and grasping for profit.

units.zh: 歷尚書殿中郎。
units.en: He served as attendant gentleman in the Secretariat.
units.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 太宗泰始中，為太子右衞率，加給事中。
units.en: During the Taishi era under Emperor Ming he was made right leader of the heir apparent's guard and additionally appointed supervisor in attendance.
units.literal: In the Taishi era of Taizong he was made Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard, with additional appointment as Supervisor in Attendance.

units.zh: 時欲北討，使勃還鄉里募人，多受貨賄。
units.en: When a northern campaign was planned, Bo was sent home to recruit troops and accepted many bribes.
units.literal: At the time a northern campaign was planned, and Bo was sent back to his home district to recruit men; he accepted many bribes.

units.zh: 上怒，下詔曰：「沈勃琴書藝業，口有美稱，而輕躁耽酒，幼多罪愆。
units.en: The emperor was enraged and issued an edict: "Shen Bo's skill in zither and letters has won him a fine reputation, yet he is rash, given to drink, and has committed many offenses since youth.
units.literal: The Emperor was angry and issued an edict, saying, "Shen Bo's zither and literary arts have won fair praise by word of mouth, yet he is flighty, addicted to wine, and from youth has committed many offenses.

units.zh: 比奢淫過度，妓女數十，聲酣放縱，無復劑限。
units.en: Lately his extravagance has gone to excess: he keeps dozens of courtesans and indulges in music and revelry without restraint.
units.literal: Recently his extravagance and debauchery have gone to excess: he keeps dozens of courtesans, and with music and revelry he gives free rein without limit.

units.zh: 自恃吳興土豪，比門義故，脅說士庶，告索無已。
units.en: Trusting in his standing as a local magnate of Wuxing and on obligations throughout his clan, he coerced gentry and commoners and extorted payment without end.
units.literal: Relying on his standing as a local magnate of Wuxing and on ties of obligation throughout his clan, he coerces and persuades gentry and commoners, demanding payment without end.

units.zh: 又輒聽募將，委役還私，託注病叛，遂有數百。
units.en: He also repeatedly let recruited officers leave duty for private affairs, falsely registering illness and desertion, until several hundred had done so.
units.literal: He also repeatedly allowed recruited officers to leave service for private affairs, falsely registering illness and desertion, until there were several hundred.

units.zh: 周旋門生，競受財貨，少者至萬，多者千金，考計贓物，二百餘萬，便宜明罰敕法，以正典刑。
units.en: His retainers and students vied to accept bribes—some as little as ten thousand cash, others a thousand in gold. The illicit goods totaled more than two million. The law should be applied clearly and the statutory punishment carried out.
units.literal: Among his retainers and students, all vied to accept goods: the least received ten thousand, the most a thousand in gold. When the illicit goods were reckoned, they exceeded two million. Let the law be clearly applied and the canonical punishment carried out.

units.zh: 故光祿大夫演之昔受深遇，忠績在朝，尋遠矜懷，能無弘律，可徙勃西垂，令一思愆悔。」
units.en: The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yanzhi once received deep favor, and his loyal service is on record at court; remembering him from afar moves one to compassion—can the law not be broadened? Let Bo be exiled to the western marches, that he may reflect and repent."
units.literal: The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Yanzhi once received deep favor, and his loyal service is recorded at court; thinking of him from afar moves one to compassion—can the law not be broadened? Bo may be exiled to the western marches, that he may once reflect and repent."

units.zh: 於是徙付梁州。
units.en: He was then exiled to Liang Province.
units.literal: Thereupon he was exiled and sent to Liang Province.

units.zh: 廢帝元徽初，以例得還。
units.en: Early in the Yuanhui era under the Deposed Emperor, he was allowed to return by precedent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, by precedent he was allowed to return.

units.zh: 結事阮佃夫、王道隆等，復為司徒左長史。
units.en: He allied himself with Ruan Tiantian, Wang Daolong, and others and again became left chief clerk of the minister over the masses.
units.literal: He attached himself to Ruan Tiantian, Wang Daolong, and others, and again became Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 為廢帝所誅。
units.en: He was put to death by the Deposed Emperor.
units.literal: He was executed by the Deposed Emperor.

units.zh: 順帝即位，追贈本官。
units.en: When Emperor Shun came to the throne, Bo's former office was posthumously restored.
units.literal: When Emperor Shun took the throne, his former office was posthumously restored.

units.zh: 勃弟統，大明中為著作佐郎。
units.en: Bo's younger brother Tong served as assistant gentleman of writings under Daming.
units.literal: Bo's younger brother Tong, in the Daming era was Assistant Gentleman of Writings.

units.zh: 先是，五省官所給幹僮，不得雜役，太祖世，坐以免官者，前後百人。
units.en: Earlier, the dry servants assigned to officials of the five directorates were forbidden to perform miscellaneous labor. Under Emperor Wen, about a hundred officials were dismissed for violating this rule.
units.literal: Earlier, the dry servants given to officials of the five directorates could not do miscellaneous labor; in the Taizu era those dismissed from office for this numbered a hundred before and after.

units.zh: 統輕役過差，有司奏免。
units.en: Tong overworked his servants beyond what was allowed, and the authorities memorialized for his dismissal.
units.literal: Tong overused his assigned servants beyond the limit; the responsible offices memorialized dismissal.

units.zh: 世祖詔曰：「自頃幹僮，多不祗給，主可量聽行杖。」
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu decreed, "Lately dry servants have often failed in their duties. Masters may, within reason, apply the staff to them."
units.literal: Shizu issued an edict: "Lately dry servants have mostly failed to attend to their duties; masters may, as a measure, be permitted to apply the staff."

units.zh: 得行幹杖，自此始也。
units.en: Permission to beat dry servants began from that time.
units.literal: Permission to apply staff to dry servants—from this it began.

units.zh: 演之兄融之子暢之，襲寧新縣男。
units.en: Changzhi, son of Yanzhi's elder brother Rongzhi, inherited the barony of Ningxin.
units.literal: Yanzhi's elder brother Rongzhi's son Changzhi inherited the barony of Ningxin county.

units.zh: 大明中，為海陵王休茂北中郎諮議參軍，為休茂所殺，追贈黃門郎。
units.en: Under Daming he served Prince Hailing Xiumao as advising colonel of the northern army and was killed by the prince. He was posthumously made gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: In the Daming era he was Advising Colonel to Prince of Hailing Xiumao as Northern Army and was killed by Xiumao; posthumously given Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 子曄嗣，齊受禪，國除。
units.en: His son Ye succeeded him; when Qi took the throne, the fief was abolished.
units.literal: His son Ye succeeded; when Qi received the mandate, the state was abolished.

units.zh: 史臣曰：元嘉初，誅滅宰相，蓋王華、孔甯子之力也。
units.en: The historian writes: At the beginning of Yuanjia the destruction of the chief ministers was largely the work of Wang Hua and Kong Ningzi.
units.literal: The historian says: At the beginning of Yuanjia the execution and destruction of chief ministers was largely the doing of Wang Hua and Kong Ningzi.

units.zh: 彼群公義雖往結，恩實今疏，而任即曩權，意非昔主，居上六之窮爻，當來寵之要轍，顛覆所基，非待他釁，況於廢殺之重，其隙易乘乎！
units.en: Those lords still had old ties of justice, but imperial favor had grown thin. They held yesterday's power without yesterday's standing with the throne. They stood in the exhausted position of the upper sixth line, on the very verge of losing favor. The ground for overturning them needed no other pretext—and how much more when the issue was execution! The opening was easy to seize.
units.literal: Those dukes in justice had past bonds but in grace were now distant; their office was yesterday's power, their mind not yesterday's lord—standing in the exhausted hexagram above six, at the critical track of coming favor, the foundation of overturning needed no other opening; how much more when the weight is execution and ruin—the gap is easy to ride!

units.zh: 夫殺人而取其璧，不知在己興累；
units.en: To kill a man and take his jade disc, unaware of the trouble one raises for oneself;
units.literal: To kill a man and take his jade disc, not knowing the trouble raised in oneself;

units.zh: 傾物而移其寵，不忌自我難持。
units.en: to overturn the established order and shift imperial favor, heedless of how hard it will be to hold one's own position.
units.literal: to overturn things and shift favor, not fearing difficulty in holding oneself.

units.zh: 若二子永年，亦未知來禍所止也。
units.en: Had those two men lived out their years, who can say where later disaster would have ended?
units.literal: If the two men had lived out their years, one still would not know where coming calamity would stop.

units.zh: 有能戒彼而悟此，則所望於來哲。
units.en: If later men can take warning from their example and understand this lesson, that is what the historian hopes for.
units.literal: If one can warn of that and awaken to this, that is what is hoped from coming sages.

units.zh: 以本官為太尉長兼行參軍，領眾二千，隨益州刺史朱齡石伐蜀。
units.en: Retaining his original rank, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand men under Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi in the campaign against Shu.
units.literal: Retaining his original office, he served as Clerk of the Grand Commandant with concurrent status as Acting Adjutant, leading two thousand troops following Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu.

units.zh: 鍾于時腳疾不能行，齡石乃詣鍾謀曰：「今天時盛熱，而賊嚴兵固險，攻之未必可拔，祗增疲困。
units.en: Zhong was then afflicted with a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi came to consult him. "The weather is fiercely hot," he said, "and the enemy holds strong positions with a tight defense. An assault may not succeed and will only wear our men down.
units.literal: Zhong at the time had a foot ailment and could not walk; Lingshi then went to Zhong to consult, saying: "Today the season is fiercely hot, and the enemy holds troops firm in strong positions; an attack may not necessarily succeed and will only increase exhaustion.

units.zh: 計其人情恇撓，必不久安，且欲養銳息兵，以伺其隙；
units.en: I reckon their troops are timid and restless and will not hold firm for long. We should conserve our strength, rest the army, and wait for an opening;
units.literal: I calculate that their men's spirits are timid and unsettled and will not long remain steady; moreover we should nurture sharpness and rest the army to watch for an opening;

units.zh: 隙而乘之，乃可捷事。
units.en: and when the moment comes, strike— that is how we can win quickly.
units.literal: when an opening appears, seize it, and then the affair can be swiftly concluded.

units.zh: 然決機兩陳，公本有所委，卿意謂何？」
units.en: Two plans are before us, and the lord originally entrusted this decision to you— what is your view?"
units.literal: Yet two plans for decision are set forth; the lord originally had someone entrusted— what does your view say?"

units.zh: 江陵平定，仍隨朱齡石伐蜀，為前鋒，由外水至于彭模，去成都二百里。
units.en: After Jiangling was pacified he again followed Zhu Lingshi against Shu as vanguard, taking the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.
units.literal: After Jiangling was pacified, he again followed Zhu Lingshi to campaign against Shu as vanguard, going by the outer water route to Pengmo, two hundred li from Chengdu.

units.zh: 齡石從之。
units.en: Lingshi accepted his counsel.
units.literal: Lingshi followed his advice.

units.zh: 郡人黃公生、任肅之、張石之等竝譙縱餘燼，與姻親侯攬、羅奧等招引白水氐，規欲為亂。
units.en: Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others in the commandery were remnants of Qiao Zong's revolt; with relatives Hou Lan and Luo Ao they stirred up the Baishui Di and plotted rebellion.
units.literal: Huang Gongsheng, Ren Suzhi, Zhang Shizhi, and others of the commandery were all embers left from Qiao Zong's rebellion; with kinsmen Hou Lan, Luo Ao, and others they recruited the Baishui Di and plotted revolt.

units.zh: 元年，除寧遠將軍、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。
units.en: In the first year of Yuanjia (424) he was appointed General of Distant Pacification and concurrent administrator of Baxi and Zitong.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia he was made General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
